finding.claim: The /mirror endpoint fetches a user-supplied URL after a host check that is a bare string suffix match. `host.endswith("example.com")` has no leading dot, so any attacker-registered domain ending in `example.com` passes (e.g. `evilexample.com`, `attacker-example.com`). The defined `ALLOWED_SUFFIX = ".example.com"` is never used. The scheme and port are not restricted, and the resolved IP is not checked against private ranges. An attacker can register such a domain and point its DNS at 169.254.169.254, localhost or internal services (or rebind DNS) to make the server request internal resources. The response length is returned, which gives a blind or semi-blind oracle.
finding.source: Query parameter `url` of GET /mirror (mirror.py:11), fully attacker-controlled

trace.note: `url` is taken from the request query string
Check `host.endswith("example.com")` with no dot boundary. Passes for `evilexample.com`. `ALLOWED_SUFFIX` on line 7 is unused.
Response body length is returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: Host suffix check at line 13 is flawed because it lacks the leading dot and does not compare against the exact host. There is no scheme allowlist, no port restriction, no DNS resolution or private-IP/link-local blocking, and no check against DNS rebinding. httpx does not follow redirects by default, which limits redirect-based bypass. The /ping endpoint uses a hardcoded URL and is not vulnerable.

verdict.guard_found: host.endswith("example.com") at mirror.py:13 (suffix check, no dot boundary; does not close). No scheme/port/IP checks; no middleware.
verdict.reason: mirror.py:11 takes attacker-controlled `url`, mirror.py:13 only does a bare endswith("example.com") that passes evilexample.com, and mirror.py:16 fetches the URL with no other guard, returning len(r.text) at line 17.
